## Backups that cost nothing. Restores you can trust.

<!-- badges:start: generated by docs/scripts/catalog.ts from the brand repo's docs/badges.md rules. -->

Most backup plugins zip your whole server every time: slow, big, and a long freeze while they save. **xBackup stores only what changed since the last backup, down to single chunks.** Hourly backups take almost no disk, and the server pauses for milliseconds.

**[Read the docs](https://plugins.xenastudios.co/xbackup/)** · **[Report a bug](https://github.com/xena-studios/plugins/issues/new/choose)**

---

## Why server owners pick it

- **Every feature free.** No premium version, no early-access builds, nothing behind a Patreon.
- **Only what changed.** Edit one chunk and the next backup stores one chunk, not an 8 MB region file. Everything is stored once, however many backups use it, so a day of hourly backups costs about what changed that day, not 24 copies of the server.
- **You won't feel it running.** Autosave goes off, the worlds are written to disk, xBackup reads what changed, and autosave goes back on: 15 to 45 ms on the server's thread in our tests on Paper. Hashing, compressing and uploading happen off the server's threads. `/backup status` shows the real pause for every backup.
- **A restore you can trust.** Every file comes back checked against the hash it was saved with. You see what a restore will change before it happens, and it never writes over a running world: it's swapped in on the next start, before any world loads.
- **Databases copied safely.** SQLite databases (block loggers, economies, any plugin's) are copied by SQLite itself, never as raw bytes, so a backup never holds a half-written database.
- **Every change applies on reload**, schedules and remotes included. No restarts.
- **Paper and Folia.** One jar runs on Paper, Purpur and Folia.

---

## What it does

- **Backups on a schedule**, every hour by default, counted from the last one so restarts don't reset it, and skipped when nobody has been online.
- **Retention that makes sense:** the newest few, then one an hour for a day, a day for a week, a week for a month and a month for six months. Pin a backup to keep it forever, cap the space backups may use, and always leave free space on the disk.
- **Copies off the server:** a second disk, S3 (AWS, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, Wasabi, MinIO), WebDAV (Nextcloud), SFTP, FTP/FTPS, Google Drive, OneDrive and Dropbox. Only new files are sent, and you can restore straight from a remote.
- **Checked, always:** each backup reads back what it wrote, a share of older data is checked every week, and `/backup verify full` checks everything.
- **Built to survive a crash.** Nothing in a repository is ever changed in place, so a crash, a power cut or a full disk mid-backup leaves every earlier backup whole.
- **A developer API** for other plugins: run a backup, add a folder, skip a backup during an event.

---

## What your staff get

- `/backup now`, `/backup list` and `/backup status`: back up, see every backup, and see how long the server paused.
- `/backup restore latest world` shows what would change; one click stages it for the next start. Or restore one plugin's folder, or one file.
- `/backup pin`, `/backup prune`, `/backup verify` and `/backup copy <remote>`.
- **From the command line** when the server won't start: `java -jar xbackup-1.0.0.jar restore latest`, or `--remote offsite` when the disk is gone.

Each subcommand has its own permission, `xbackup.<subcommand>`, all op-only until you give them out, so a helper with `xbackup.list` and `xbackup.status` can look without changing anything.

---

## Up and running in a minute

1. Drop the jar in `plugins/` and start the server. It backs up every hour into `plugins/xBackup/repository`.
2. Run `/backup now`, then `/backup status`.
3. Add a remote in `plugins/xBackup/config.yml`, so a copy lives somewhere else, and run `/xbackup reload`.

Full setup, every setting, every remote and how to restore: **[plugins.xenastudios.co/xbackup](https://plugins.xenastudios.co/xbackup/)**

**Requires** Paper 1.21.11 or newer (or Purpur or Folia) and Java 21 or newer. Nothing else.
